subject: Pilot scout: multi-locale evaluation & mitigation plan
messages:

Subject: Pilot scout: multi-locale evaluation & mitigation plan

Hi Anna — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick post-call summary, recommended next steps, and the artifacts I promised. Keeping this high level so the procurement and engineering teams can pick the right pilot scope.

TL;DR
- We propose a 6-week pilot: focused evaluation across 3 EU languages (FR, DE, NL) and 2 APAC locales (JA, KO).
- Deliverables: evaluation report, prompt bundle for production testset, a lightweight SOW and preliminary cost bands.

What we heard on the call
- Primary product integration is the clinician-facing summarization flow and triage suggestions (short text -> structured output).
- Primary concerns: hallucination around medication names (JP/KO), style/verbosity in FR/DE, and tokenization/stop-word handling in NL.
- Success criteria: human-rated adequacy >= 4/5 on sampled testsets, hallucination rate < 3% on entity checks, and median inference latency < 220ms for the interactive path.

Initial model recommendations (for pilot)
- Candidate A (latency-first): llama-2-13b-chat-quantized (q4f16) — good latency with instruction-following, recommend for interactive demo.
- Candidate B (quality-first): open-multilingual-13b (fp16) — better cross-lingual fidelity on our evals; heavier but useful for offline batch scoring.
- Fallback: distilled-mt-7b (q4) — low-cost baseline for high-volume routing.

Evaluation plan highlights
- Automatic: BLEU/ROUGE only as cursory signals — we’ll use cross-lingual semantic similarity (multilingual embeddings) and entity F1 for medication/person names.
- Human: native-speaker rating panel (fluency, adequacy, hallucination, safety) per locale (n=120 samples/locale).
- Regression watchlist: we’ll track hallucination spikes by entity type and prompt changes; set automated alerts if entity F1 drops by >6% from baseline.

Attachments and links
- Attached: pilot_scope_v1.pdf (scope, milestones), prompt_bundle_eu_apac.zip (starter prompts + sanity tests), benchmark_snapshot_20260912.csv (our preliminary sandbox runs).
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3CEXAMPLE (evaluation folder)

Next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm the five pilot languages and primary test sets (we noted FR/DE/NL/JA/KO)?
2) Procurement: confirm if a 6-week paid pilot is acceptable or if you need a shorter paid POC. Procurement contacts cc’d.
3) Engineering: please share any data retention / KMS constraints up front — we’ll include that in the Private deployment options.

If that looks good I’ll send a short SOW + calendar for a kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0198

Folks — forwarding Anna’s reply. Action items for our side below.

On Tue, 14 Sep 2026 at 14:18 +0200 Anna Lopez <anna@linguahealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Rafael — thanks for the clear summary. This aligns with our thinking. ...
> We are interested in the model candidates you suggested; please indicate which one you recommend for the shorter 4-week upfront pilot.

Internal ask (short):
- Recommend a single model for 4-week pilot (tradeoff: show value quickly vs avoid hallucination risk). My suggestion: start with llama-2-13b-chat-quantized (q4f16) as the demo model because it gives a good interactive experience with lower infra cost; run open-multilingual-13b in parallel for offline scoring on a smaller sample to detect quality delta.
- Pricing: prepare two cost bands (hosted API vs Dedicated reserved for 4 weeks). I’ll need a rough draft for pricing to send to procurement by EOD Wednesday.
- Compliance: Aditya — confirm we can commit to customer-managed KMS for the pilot and list any lead times.

Risk matrix (short-hand)
- FR/DE: quality variance (tone/verbosity) — mitigate with locale-specific prompt templates and a 30-sample style tuning pass.
- NL: tokenization / stop-words — mitigate with token-level checks and small rule-based post-processing.
- JA/KO: hallucination on medication names — add entity-level validators and expand KEV (known entity vocabulary) prior to human eval.

Deliverable timeline (suggested)
- Day 0–5: kickoff, dataset handoff, SOW signed
- Week 1–2: sandbox runs + automatic metrics + prompt bundle iteration
- Week 3: native-speaker human evaluation (120 samples/locale)
- Week 4: consolidated pilot report + handoff + decision meeting

I’ll draft the pricing bands and the short SOW; Marissa please coordinate the sales-facing summary and Aditya confirm KMS details.

Thanks,
Rafael
